questions.questionText: Your company wants to measure the actual performance of an application deployed on Google Cloud to ensure it is meeting user expectations. They have decided to track the ratio of successful HTTP requests to total HTTP requests. Which operational concept does this specific measurement represent?

explanation.general explanation: A Service Level Indicator (SLI) is a carefully defined quantitative measure of some aspect of the level of service that is provided. Tracking the ratio of successful HTTP requests to total requests is a classic example of an availability SLI.

why other options are wrong.Service Level Agreement (SLA): An SLA is a contractual agreement with business consequences if targets are missed, not the raw measurement itself.
why other options are wrong.Service Level Objective (SLO): An SLO is a target value or range of values for a service level that is measured by an SLI, such as '99.9% availability', not the measurement ratio itself.
why other options are wrong.Key Performance Indicator (KPI): While an SLI can inform a KPI, a KPI is typically a broader business metric, whereas an SLI is a specific technical measurement of service reliability.

questions.questionText: Your organization has migrated its e-commerce platform to Google Cloud. The executive team wants to ensure that the platform maintains high availability and has set a target that 99.95% of all user requests must succeed within a 30-day window. What does this target represent?

explanation.general explanation: A Service Level Objective (SLO) specifies a target level for the reliability of your service. It acts as an internal goal (e.g., 99.95% availability) that the engineering team strives to meet to ensure user satisfaction.

why other options are wrong.Service Level Agreement (SLA): An SLA is an external, contractual promise made to customers that often includes financial penalties if the SLA is breached.
why other options are wrong.Service Level Indicator (SLI): An SLI is the actual measurement of the service's performance, such as the current real-time percentage of successful requests, rather than the target itself.
why other options are wrong.Return on Investment (ROI): ROI is a financial metric used to evaluate the profitability or financial efficiency of an investment, not an operational reliability target.

questions.questionText: A SaaS provider hosts its application on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). They offer enterprise customers a contract stating that if application uptime falls below 99.9% in a given month, the customer will receive a 10% credit on their next bill. Which operational success metric does this contract represent?

explanation.general explanation: A Service Level Agreement (SLA) is an explicit or implicit contract with users that includes consequences (such as financial credits or penalties) if the service fails to meet its promised reliability targets.

why other options are wrong.Service Level Objective (SLO): An SLO is an internal target level of reliability. Missing an SLO informs engineering priorities but does not inherently trigger financial penalties.
why other options are wrong.Service Level Indicator (SLI): An SLI is the actual metric used to measure performance, not the contractual agreement.
why other options are wrong.Error Budget: An error budget is the acceptable amount of unreliability allowed before a system breaches its SLO. It is an internal engineering management tool.

questions.questionText: Your company is planning a cloud migration and wants to define success measurements from a financial perspective. The Chief Financial Officer (CFO) asks you to calculate the comprehensive financial impact over a 5-year period, including initial migration costs, operational costs, software licenses, and expected cost reductions. Which financial measurement is the CFO asking for?

explanation.general explanation: Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) is a comprehensive financial estimate that evaluates all direct and indirect costs associated with a system over its entire lifecycle or a specific forecasting period, such as 5 years.

why other options are wrong.Return on Investment (ROI): While ROI calculates the financial gain relative to the investment cost, TCO specifically calculates the absolute total sum of all costs incurred over time.
why other options are wrong.Capital Expenditure (CapEx): CapEx refers only to the upfront costs to acquire physical assets (like on-premise hardware), whereas TCO includes CapEx, OpEx, and indirect costs.
why other options are wrong.Service Level Objective (SLO): An SLO is an operational reliability metric, not a financial measurement.

questions.questionText: An engineering team uses error budgets to manage the reliability of their application on Google Cloud. If the service breaches its defined error budget for the month, what is the standard SRE best practice for the team's next steps?
options: Halt all new feature rollouts and focus engineering efforts exclusively on reliability and stability.
Increase the Service Level Objective (SLO) to ensure the budget is not breached again.
Ignore the breach if it does not violate the customer Service Level Agreement (SLA).
Scale up the compute resources horizontally to immediately resolve any underlying code bugs.
correctAnswers: Halt all new feature rollouts and focus engineering efforts exclusively on reliability and stability.

explanation.general explanation: The primary purpose of an error budget is to balance feature velocity with reliability. When the error budget is depleted, the standard Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) practice is to freeze new feature releases and focus the team entirely on fixing reliability issues until the budget resets.

why other options are wrong.Increase the Service Level Objective (SL: Artificially changing the target simply to avoid a breach defeats the purpose of having an SLO. The SLO should reflect true business and user needs.
why other options are wrong.Ignore the breach if it does not violate: SLOs are intentionally stricter than SLAs. Ignoring an SLO breach puts the service at high risk of eventually breaching the SLA and causing financial penalties.
why other options are wrong.Scale up the compute resources horizonta: Scaling infrastructure handles load but does not fix underlying application code bugs or architectural reliability issues.

questions.questionText: When establishing success measurements for a newly deployed business-critical application, why is it considered a best practice for your internal Service Level Objective (SLO) to be stricter than your external Service Level Agreement (SLA)?
options: To provide an internal buffer that allows engineering teams to detect and fix issues before they result in SLA financial penalties.
To ensure that customers are legally bound to accept more downtime than they initially expected.
Because Google Cloud requires SLOs to be mathematically twice as stringent as any SLA hosted on its infrastructure.
Because SLAs only measure infrastructure availability, whereas SLOs measure only application logic errors.
correctAnswers: To provide an internal buffer that allows engineering teams to detect and fix issues before they result in SLA financial penalties.

explanation.general explanation: Setting a stricter SLO than the external SLA creates a safety margin. If an internal SLO is breached, engineers can react and stabilize the system before the downtime exceeds the looser limits set in the contractual SLA, thereby avoiding financial penalties.

why other options are wrong.To ensure that customers are legally bou: The SLA defines the legal terms, not the internal SLO. Stricter SLOs do not change the legal SLA terms.
why other options are wrong.Because Google Cloud requires SLOs to be: Google Cloud provides SRE best practices but does not dictate or enforce internal corporate SLO metrics mathematically.
why other options are wrong.Because SLAs only measure infrastructure: Both SLAs and SLOs can measure a wide variety of metrics, including availability, latency, and throughput, across both infrastructure and application layers.

questions.questionText: Your team is defining Service Level Indicators (SLIs) for a user-facing HTTP web application hosted on Cloud Run. Which of the following metrics is the MOST appropriate SLI for measuring the latency of this web application?
options: The 99th percentile of response times for all successful HTTP GET requests.
The average CPU utilization of the Cloud Run instances over a 24-hour period.
The total number of HTTP 5xx errors returned to the client per day.
The total amount of network bandwidth consumed by the application per minute.
correctAnswers: The 99th percentile of response times for all successful HTTP GET requests.

explanation.general explanation: Latency SLIs should measure the time it takes to return a response to the user. Using the 99th percentile (p99) is a standard SRE best practice because it accurately reflects the experience of the slowest requests, avoiding the masking effect of simple averages.

why other options are wrong.The average CPU utilization of the Cloud: CPU utilization is an infrastructure metric, not an indicator of user-facing latency. High CPU doesn't always strictly equate to high latency.
why other options are wrong.The total number of HTTP 5xx errors retu: This is a measure of availability or error rate, not latency.
why other options are wrong.The total amount of network bandwidth co: This measures throughput or network consumption, which does not directly indicate how fast the application is responding to individual user requests.

questions.questionText: A media company has adopted an Agile methodology alongside its Google Cloud migration. The business wants to measure whether moving to GCP has actually improved developer velocity and time-to-market. Which success measurement should they track?

explanation.general explanation: Deployment frequency is a core DORA (DevOps Research and Assessment) metric. An increase in how often code is successfully deployed to production directly indicates improved developer velocity and faster time-to-market.

why other options are wrong.Mean Time To Detect (MTTD): MTTD measures how quickly the team spots an operational incident. It is a reliability and monitoring metric, not a measure of developer velocity.
why other options are wrong.Database transaction throughput: This is an infrastructure performance metric, not a direct measure of business time-to-market or developer velocity.
why other options are wrong.Total Cost of Ownership (TCO): TCO measures financial cost, not the speed at which new features are delivered to end users.

questions.questionText: A company is designing a Disaster Recovery (DR) plan on Google Cloud. The business has specified that in the event of a total regional outage, the system must be restored and operational within 4 hours. Which success measurement does this 4-hour target represent?

explanation.general explanation: The Recovery Time Objective (RTO) is the targeted duration of time and a service level within which a business process must be restored after a disaster. A 4-hour RTO means the system must be back online 4 hours after an outage begins.

why other options are wrong.Recovery Point Objective (RPO): RPO defines the maximum acceptable amount of data loss measured in time, not the time it takes to restore the system's operational status.
why other options are wrong.Mean Time To Resolve (MTTR): MTTR is an operational metric representing the average time taken to fully resolve an incident. While related, RTO is a specific upper-bound target for disaster recovery planning.
why other options are wrong.Service Level Indicator (SLI): An SLI is a measure of standard service performance (like latency or availability), not a metric specifically defining disaster recovery restoration time targets.

questions.questionText: Which two metrics are essential for calculating the current status of an Error Budget for a specific Google Cloud service? (Select two)

explanation.general explanation: An Error Budget is calculated by taking 100% and subtracting the Service Level Objective (SLO). To know how much of that budget has been consumed, you must continually measure the actual system performance using a Service Level Indicator (SLI).

why other options are wrong.Recovery Time Objective (RTO): RTO is a disaster recovery metric denoting maximum acceptable downtime duration, not a component used to calculate rolling error budgets.
why other options are wrong.Total Cost of Ownership (TCO): TCO is a financial metric and is entirely unrelated to operational reliability error budgets.

questions.questionText: An enterprise is adopting Cloud FinOps to better manage its Google Cloud billing. The team wants a success metric that proves they are optimizing their application architectures over time as user traffic grows. Which success metric best demonstrates architectural cost efficiency?
options: Total overall monthly Google Cloud bill
Amount of committed use discounts purchased
Number of Virtual Machines running concurrently

explanation.general explanation: Unit cost measures the cost required to deliver a specific unit of business value (like a transaction or a user session). If user traffic grows, the total bill might increase, but if the unit cost stays the same or decreases, it proves the architecture is cost-efficient and scaling optimally.

why other options are wrong.Total overall monthly Google Cloud bill: A rising total bill is normal if business traffic is growing. Total bill alone does not indicate whether the architecture is efficient.
why other options are wrong.Amount of committed use discounts purcha: Purchasing discounts is a procurement strategy, not a metric indicating architectural efficiency or optimization.
why other options are wrong.Number of Virtual Machines running concu: More VMs might be needed for higher traffic. Counting VMs does not measure financial efficiency or business value.

questions.questionText: A healthcare provider has implemented a new internal dashboard on Google Cloud for nurses to track patient vitals. The project sponsor wants to measure the internal user adoption of the new tool as a primary success criteria. Which measurement is most appropriate?

explanation.general explanation: Daily Active Users (DAU) is a standard key performance indicator (KPI) for measuring product adoption and user engagement. It tells the business exactly how many nurses are actively using the new dashboard every day.

why other options are wrong.Mean Time To Recovery (MTTR): MTTR measures incident response speed, not whether users are actually adopting the tool.
why other options are wrong.Page load latency: Latency measures performance. While good performance aids adoption, latency itself does not measure user adoption.
why other options are wrong.Database storage capacity consumed: Storage capacity is an infrastructure metric. A high capacity could be due to automated data ingestion rather than active human user engagement.

questions.questionText: A financial analytics company migrates its nightly batch processing pipelines from on-premises Hadoop to Google Cloud Dataproc. They want to define a Service Level Indicator (SLI) to measure the reliability of this pipeline. Which SLI is most appropriate for a batch processing system?

explanation.general explanation: For batch processing pipelines, success is typically measured by how much data can be processed within a specific time window. Throughput (bytes or records processed per minute) is the standard SLI for assessing batch system performance and reliability.

why other options are wrong.HTTP 200 OK response rates: This is an availability metric for synchronous web services/APIs, not asynchronous batch pipelines.
why other options are wrong.User session duration: This measures user engagement on a frontend application, which is irrelevant for a backend batch job.
why other options are wrong.Cache hit ratio: This measures the efficiency of a caching layer (like Cloud CDN or Memorystore), not the performance of a Hadoop/Dataproc batch pipeline.

questions.questionText: Your company sets a goal to resolve any P1 (Critical) incidents within 30 minutes of detection. Which operational success metric does this goal represent?

explanation.general explanation: Mean Time To Resolve (MTTR) is a metric that tracks the average amount of time required to fully resolve a system failure or incident and restore standard operations.

why other options are wrong.Mean Time To Detect (MTTD): MTTD measures how long it takes an organization to discover a problem, not how long it takes to fix it.
why other options are wrong.Recovery Point Objective (RPO): RPO is the acceptable amount of data loss during a disaster, measured in time. It is not an incident resolution time metric.
why other options are wrong.Service Level Agreement (SLA): An SLA is a formal contract between a service provider and a customer. While an SLA might contain an MTTR clause, the 30-minute goal itself is an MTTR target.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is considered a poor choice for a Service Level Indicator (SLI) to measure user-facing application availability?
options: Average CPU utilization of backend virtual machines
The percentage of successful HTTP responses (2xx and 3xx)
The number of completed user login flows divided by attempted logins
The error rate reported by the external load balancer
correctAnswers: Average CPU utilization of backend virtual machines

explanation.general explanation: Good SLIs measure the service from the perspective of the user. CPU utilization is an internal infrastructure metric. A high CPU utilization does not necessarily mean the application is unavailable, and low CPU does not guarantee the application is working.

why other options are wrong.The percentage of successful HTTP respon: This is a direct, excellent SLI for measuring the availability of web services as it reflects what the user receives.
why other options are wrong.The number of completed user login flows: This is an excellent business-level SLI that directly measures a critical user journey.
why other options are wrong.The error rate reported by the external: Load balancers sit very close to the user and their error rates are excellent indicators of perceived availability.

questions.questionText: You are migrating a monolithic application to microservices on Google Cloud. You want to measure the success of the Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) culture adoption. A key tenet of SRE is reducing 'toil'. What is the best way to measure a reduction in toil?
options: Tracking the decrease in time spent by engineers on manual, repetitive operational tasks.
Measuring the reduction in the total number of physical servers managed by the team.
Tracking the increase in the number of open support tickets logged by customers.
Measuring the amount of error budget consumed per month.
correctAnswers: Tracking the decrease in time spent by engineers on manual, repetitive operational tasks.

explanation.general explanation: In SRE terms, 'toil' refers to operational work that is manual, repetitive, automatable, tactical, devoid of enduring value, and scales linearly as a service grows. Measuring success in reducing toil involves tracking the time engineers save by automating these specific tasks.

why other options are wrong.Measuring the reduction in the total num: While cloud migration reduces physical server management, toil applies to any repetitive operational task, including managing cloud resources.
why other options are wrong.Tracking the increase in the number of o: An increase in support tickets is a negative outcome and indicates poor reliability, not a reduction in toil.
why other options are wrong.Measuring the amount of error budget con: Error budget consumption measures service reliability, not the amount of manual work (toil) engineers are performing.

questions.questionText: Your company wants to integrate environmental sustainability into its success measurements for its Google Cloud infrastructure. Which metric provided natively by Google Cloud is best suited to track the success of this initiative?

explanation.general explanation: Google Cloud provides a Carbon Footprint tool that natively reports the gross carbon emissions associated with an organization's Google Cloud usage. This is the direct metric used to measure environmental sustainability success in the cloud.

why other options are wrong.Committed Use Discount utilization: This is a financial success metric used for cost optimization, not environmental sustainability.
why other options are wrong.Network Egress bandwidth volume: While high bandwidth consumes resources, tracking raw bytes does not translate directly into a measurable sustainability or emissions metric without the Carbon Footprint tool.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Identity active user count: This measures user adoption and identity management scale, completely unrelated to environmental sustainability.

questions.questionText: You are assessing the success of a newly implemented auto-scaling strategy for Managed Instance Groups (MIGs) on Google Compute Engine. The business goal is to handle traffic spikes without over-provisioning resources. Which two metrics provide the best indication of success? (Select two)
options: Application latency during peak traffic hours
Average CPU utilization across the MIG
Total data stored in Cloud SQL
The number of Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles assigned
correctAnswers: Application latency during peak traffic hours
Average CPU utilization across the MIG

explanation.general explanation: A successful auto-scaling strategy maintains performance (preventing high latency during spikes) while maintaining cost efficiency (keeping average CPU utilization close to the target threshold, ensuring resources aren't sitting idle). Tracking both latency and utilization proves the MIG is scaling correctly.

why other options are wrong.Total data stored in Cloud SQL: Database storage volume does not indicate whether compute instances are auto-scaling efficiently.
why other options are wrong.The number of Identity and Access Manage: IAM role counts are related to security and access control, not auto-scaling performance or efficiency.

questions.questionText: A media streaming company is using Cloud CDN to serve video content globally. They want to define a success measurement that proves the CDN is effectively reducing the load on their backend origin servers. Which metric is most appropriate?

explanation.general explanation: The cache hit ratio measures the percentage of requests that are successfully served directly from the CDN edge cache compared to total requests. A high cache hit ratio directly indicates that fewer requests are being forwarded to the backend origin servers, proving the CDN's effectiveness.

why other options are wrong.Origin server disk write speed: Disk write speed is an I/O performance metric for the backend server itself. CDNs primarily cache read operations, not writes.
why other options are wrong.Number of HTTP 404 errors: HTTP 404 (Not Found) errors indicate broken links or missing resources, not the efficiency of the caching layer.
why other options are wrong.Database query response time: While a CDN offloads traffic, database query response time is influenced by many factors and is an indirect metric. Cache hit ratio is the direct measurement of CDN success.

questions.questionText: A corporate IT team migrates its core applications using a 'lift-and-shift' approach to Google Cloud using Migrate to Virtual Machines. During this initial migration phase, what is the most appropriate primary success measurement?
options: Identical application functionality with minimal cutover downtime.
A complete rewrite of the application code into serverless functions.
An immediate 90% reduction in database storage costs.
Achieving an active-active global multi-region deployment.
correctAnswers: Identical application functionality with minimal cutover downtime.

explanation.general explanation: A 'lift-and-shift' (rehosting) migration aims to move applications to the cloud with as few changes as possible. The primary success measurement for this phase is ensuring the application functions exactly as it did on-premises, with minimal disruption during the migration cutover.

why other options are wrong.A complete rewrite of the application co: Rewriting code is a 'refactoring' or 're-architecting' strategy, which is the opposite of a lift-and-shift migration.
why other options are wrong.An immediate 90% reduction in database s: Lift-and-shift migrations rarely yield immediate massive cost savings because the architecture remains largely unchanged; optimization usually occurs in a subsequent phase.
why other options are wrong.Achieving an active-active global multi-: Lift-and-shift moves the existing architecture. If the on-premise application was not globally active-active, a lift-and-shift will not magically make it so.

questions.questionText: A security operations team uses Security Command Center (SCC) on Google Cloud. They want to measure the success of their vulnerability management program. Which metric provides the best measurement of their operational security success?
options: Total number of firewall rules created
Number of IAM users in the organization
Volume of log data ingested into Cloud Logging

explanation.general explanation: In security operations, detecting a vulnerability is only the first step. The 'Time to patch' or 'Mean Time to Remediate' measures how quickly the team actually secures the environment after a threat is identified. This is a critical KPI for a vulnerability management program.

why other options are wrong.Total number of firewall rules created: Creating more rules does not mean the environment is more secure; in fact, overly complex firewall rules can introduce misconfigurations.
why other options are wrong.Number of IAM users in the organization: The sheer number of users is an administrative metric, not an indicator of security posture or success.
why other options are wrong.Volume of log data ingested into Cloud L: While ingesting logs is necessary for visibility, the volume of logs does not measure whether vulnerabilities are actually being addressed.

questions.questionText: Your company has a Service Level Objective (SLO) requiring 99.9% availability for a customer API. What mathematical concept defines the maximum allowable amount of downtime for this API over a specific time window?

explanation.general explanation: The Error Budget is mathematically derived from the SLO (100% minus the SLO percentage). If the SLO is 99.9% availability, the error budget is the remaining 0.1%, which represents the maximum allowable downtime or failure rate over that time window.

why other options are wrong.Service Level Agreement (SLA): An SLA is a contract outlining consequences for missing targets, not the mathematical allowance of downtime used by engineering teams.
why other options are wrong.Recovery Point Objective (RPO): RPO measures acceptable data loss during a disaster, not availability downtime allowances.
why other options are wrong.Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF): MTBF is the average time a system operates between breakdowns. It does not dictate a maximum allowable budget of downtime.

questions.questionText: A data analytics team migrates its on-premises data warehouse to BigQuery. The primary business driver was that end-of-month financial reports were taking over 24 hours to generate. Which metric should the business use as the primary success measurement for this BigQuery migration?
options: Query execution time for the end-of-month financial reports
The number of tables created in the BigQuery dataset
The number of concurrent users logged into the Google Cloud Console
The amount of data compressed during the upload process
correctAnswers: Query execution time for the end-of-month financial reports

explanation.general explanation: Success measurements must directly align with the business drivers. If the problem was that reports took 24 hours to generate, the primary metric of success is the reduction in query execution time for those specific reports in the new BigQuery environment.

why other options are wrong.The number of tables created in the BigQ: The number of tables is an architectural detail, not a measurement of performance or business value.
why other options are wrong.The number of concurrent users logged in: The number of users in the console does not indicate whether the specific reporting problem was solved.
why other options are wrong.The amount of data compressed during the: While data compression saves money in BigQuery, it does not directly measure whether the reports are generating faster.

questions.questionText: When deciding WHERE to measure a Service Level Indicator (SLI) for a user-facing web application, what is the best practice according to Google Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) principles?
options: Measure as close to the end user as possible, such as at the load balancer or client side.
Measure directly on the database instances to ensure data integrity.
Measure network latency between internal backend microservices only.
Measure the CPU utilization of the worker nodes.
correctAnswers: Measure as close to the end user as possible, such as at the load balancer or client side.

explanation.general explanation: An SLI should ideally reflect the user's actual experience. Measuring at the load balancer, API gateway, or even via client-side instrumentation provides the most accurate representation of what the user is experiencing in terms of latency and availability.

why other options are wrong.Measure directly on the database instanc: While database metrics are useful for debugging, they do not accurately reflect the overall availability or latency experienced by the end user on a web browser.
why other options are wrong.Measure network latency between internal: Internal latency is just one component. The user's request also traverses external networks, load balancers, and frontends, which would be ignored if only internal latency is measured.
why other options are wrong.Measure the CPU utilization of the worke: CPU utilization is an internal resource metric, not a measure of the user's service experience.

questions.questionText: Your team is launching a new API Gateway solution. They want to define an SLO based on a latency SLI. Which of the following is a correctly formatted Service Level Objective (SLO)?
options: 99% of successful API requests will have a response time of less than 200 milliseconds over a trailing 30-day window.
The API will utilize an average of 50% CPU and 60% Memory over the next month.
Customers will receive a 15% refund if the API is down for more than 4 hours a month.
The API Gateway will log all errors to Cloud Logging immediately.
correctAnswers: 99% of successful API requests will have a response time of less than 200 milliseconds over a trailing 30-day window.

explanation.general explanation: A properly formatted SLO combines a target percentage (99%), a specific measurable SLI (response time < 200ms for successful requests), and a defined time window (trailing 30-day window).

why other options are wrong.The API will utilize an average of 50% C: This is an infrastructure utilization target, not a reliability service level objective for users.
why other options are wrong.Customers will receive a 15% refund if t: This statement describes financial penalties, making it a Service Level Agreement (SLA), not an SLO.
why other options are wrong.The API Gateway will log all errors to C: This is a system configuration requirement, not an objective that can be measured via a percentage against a target.

questions.questionText: A multinational corporation has completely migrated its on-premises data centers to Google Cloud. As an architect, you are asked to demonstrate to the board of directors that the cloud investment has a positive financial return over time compared to the initial migration costs. Which metric should you present?

explanation.general explanation: Return on Investment (ROI) is a core financial metric used to evaluate the efficiency and profitability of an investment. It directly measures the financial return generated relative to the cost of the cloud migration.

why other options are wrong.Service Level Agreement (SLA): SLA is an external contractual reliability metric, not a financial investment metric.
why other options are wrong.Mean Time To Resolve (MTTR): MTTR is an operational metric measuring incident response speed, which does not convey financial return to a board of directors.
why other options are wrong.Daily Active Users (DAU): DAU measures product engagement. While high DAU is good, it doesn't quantify the direct financial return on the cloud infrastructure investment.

questions.questionText: An online gaming company uses Cloud Spanner to ensure real-time multiplayer state is consistent worldwide. They define a success measurement requiring global strong consistency with reads completing in single-digit milliseconds. Which Google Cloud architectural characteristic are they measuring?

explanation.general explanation: The requirement specifies 'reads completing in single-digit milliseconds' (which is a latency metric) and 'global strong consistency' (which is a data integrity/consistency metric). Cloud Spanner is specifically designed to provide exactly these two characteristics at global scale.

why other options are wrong.Disaster Recovery RTO: RTO refers to restoration time after an outage, not standard real-time read speed or consistency.
why other options are wrong.Cost per transaction: While important, the scenario specifically highlights read speeds and state consistency, not financial costs.
why other options are wrong.Network bandwidth volume: Bandwidth volume measures the amount of data transferred, not the speed (latency) or the consistency state of the database.

questions.questionText: Which two metrics are commonly used to evaluate the success of a Disaster Recovery (DR) implementation on Google Cloud? (Select two)

explanation.general explanation: Disaster Recovery strategies are fundamentally measured by two core metrics: RTO (how quickly the system must be restored) and RPO (the maximum acceptable amount of data loss, measured in time).

why other options are wrong.Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF): MTBF measures the standard operational reliability of a system over time, not the specific data loss or restoration targets during a catastrophic disaster.
why other options are wrong.Daily Active Users (DAU): DAU is a product adoption metric, entirely unrelated to disaster recovery planning.

questions.questionText: Your engineering team deploys a monitoring solution using Cloud Monitoring. They define an alert that triggers if the CPU utilization of a critical instance exceeds 90% for 5 minutes. The purpose of this alert is to catch issues before the service goes down. Which concept does the speed of this alert trigger relate to?

explanation.general explanation: Mean Time To Detect (MTTD) measures how quickly an organization becomes aware of a potential issue. Configuring fast, automated alerts in Cloud Monitoring directly reduces the MTTD, allowing teams to respond faster.

why other options are wrong.Recovery Point Objective (RPO): RPO is a disaster recovery metric relating to data loss, not alerting speed.
why other options are wrong.Mean Time To Resolve (MTTR): MTTR measures how long it takes to fix the issue once it is detected. The alert itself only covers detection (MTTD).
why other options are wrong.Service Level Agreement (SLA): An SLA is an external contract. While fast alerting helps avoid SLA breaches, the speed of the alert itself is characterized by MTTD.

questions.questionText: A retail company migrates its media assets to Google Cloud Storage. They measure success by ensuring that the files are highly protected against hardware failures and are consistently accessible globally. Which two inherent characteristics of Cloud Storage are they utilizing as success measurements? (Select two)

explanation.general explanation: When dealing with object storage like Google Cloud Storage, Durability (protection against data loss/hardware failure) and Availability (ensuring data can be accessed when requested) are the two fundamental metrics of success for data storage reliability.

why other options are wrong.Compute performance: Cloud Storage is an object storage service, not a compute service. Compute performance (like CPU speed) is irrelevant.
why other options are wrong.Relational referential integrity: Referential integrity is a concept for relational databases (like Cloud SQL or Spanner), not unstructured object storage like Cloud Storage.
